subject: meeting demo
body:
Hi Amin!

 

It was great to meet you yesterday and hear more about the Avicenna platform. We talked with our other colleagues this afternoon and are excited about the potential for data collection using your app. We would like to set up a demo/trial of the app with a few members of our research group to see how it works and test out the GPS data collection and the EMA survey set up, and perhaps some simple geofencing EMA triggers if that is possible (like to home or work locations). Would that be possible, and what would we need to do to set that up?

 

Justin (CC’d) is going to be in touch soon with a more specific list of our data collection needs, to get a more precise quote for services if we were to decide to use this platform.

 

Thanks so much, looking forward to learning more.

 

Best,

Beth

 



Bethany Boettner, PhD
Research Scientist
Institute for Population Research
65 Townshend Hall
1885 Neil Ave Mall, Columbus, OH 43210
614-292-5137 Office
boettner.6@osu.edu

Amin Tavassolian We can't add geofencing EMA triggers to their demo study, right? I am going to let them know it should be customized based on their protocol and done as part of their actual study. Can you confirm if this is OK? Additionally, should we implement their study for them or allow them to proceed with it on their own? Thank you.

Sara Farnya Yes you are correct. Just to make sure we are clear about what you said:

We can create a sample study for them to showcase the EMA part and let them collect GPS data. The geo fence triggering part requires a bit of effort on our end and it would be great if we do it as part of the actual project. They can test the geo-fence in their real study as long as they want to make sure it works exactly they way the expect. 

Ask them to share their protocol with us and we will check it. We can hold a workshop to implement their survey live as well.

body:

Thanks again for taking the time to meet with us! I have attached a document that provides the minimum requirements/capabilities that we are looking for in a data collection platform for the AHDC2 study. It would be great if we could get a price estimate for both scenarios.

If we could get a separate estimate for this as well it would be greatly appreciated.

 

We look forward to hearing from you!

 

Justin

subject: meeting demo
body:
Hi Justin and Beth,

Hope all is well with you.

It was a pleasure speaking with you the other day. We are very excited about this opportunity.

We'd be happy to set up a trial project for you to test the GPS and EMA data collection features. The geofence triggering feature will need some customization based on your specific study protocol, but we’ll ensure it’s fully set up for your real study so you can test it thoroughly before deployment. To get started, please share the questionnaires you’d like to test, and we’ll take care of the next steps. If you like, we can also arrange a live workshop for this setup.

Also, thanks a lot for sharing the details of the AHDC2 and AHDC2+ studies. Please let me review the requirements and get back to you by tomorrow.

Lastly, as promised, below are a few of our past/current projects for your reference:

  • Open Research Lab’s Basic Income Project: Avicenna is the primary technology provider for the largest Basic Income project ever conducted, with more than 3,000 participants in the US, since 2017. The project involved more than 40 investigators, and 7 institutions across the country (Every Dollar Counts app).
  • ACT Health (Australian Health Ministry) has been using Avicenna since 2019 as part of their Data Analytics Branch in the Policy, Partnerships, and Programs Division for multiple initiatives, including COVID-19 Impact, LGBTQ Challenges, and Teenager Parenting Practices (Canberra Health app, only available in Australia)
  • University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), in partnership with Apple, is using Avicenna to collect health data from Apple Watch devices to operationalize digital phenotyping in the measurement of Anhedonia. (DGC App)
  • Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) is using Avicenna to understand the role of human movement in the spread of COVID-19 and HIV in South Africa. The team is using Avicenna's custom solution, the Sesikhona app, to study more than 500 participants.
  • The Well-being project by the INTERACT team has been using Avicenna since 2016 to study the physical activity behavior of more than 7,000 Canadians across Quebec, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan.
  • The COHESION Project is using Avicenna to measure the effects and risks of COVID-19 on people's lives. Starting in late 2020 shortly after the COVID outbreak, the team leveraged Avicenna to rapidly deploy the study to more than 3,500 participants across Canada. 
  • PROTECT Me, a partnership project between TU Delft and Erasmus Medical Centre in the Netherlands is using Avicenna to develop tools that will make it possible to identify teenagers and young adults who struggle with mental health issues such as feelings of depression.
  • Vrije University’s NTR welbevinden is using Avicenna to collect a combination of active and passive data from twins aiming to find new insights about the fluctuations of well-being and happiness.
  • University of Saskatchewan Medical School's research is using Avicenna for caregivers to learn various skills that aid in self-compassion and self-care practices via our Eleos App.
I'm always available for a quick chat and my calendar is shared here.

Best,
Amin
--
Avicenna Research (formerly Ethica Data)
4109 - 295 Adelaide St W, Toronto, ON M5V 0L4, Canada
Email: sales@avicennaresearch.com - Web: https://avicennaresearch.com
